_comment: RES-006 -- recorded performance baselines. Loaded by
src/diagnostics/performance_baseline.py and checked by the nightly
These are budgets, not measurements of a particular machine. A budget is
chosen from what the trading loop needs -- a 1m bar leaves 60 seconds for
everything downstream of it, and the p99 numbers below sum to a small
fraction of that on purpose, because the interesting failure is the slow
drift that eats the margin over a release or two.
regression_tolerance is how much worse than baseline a run may be before
it fails. 0.25 = 25% slower. Tight enough to catch an accidental O(n^2),
loose enough to survive a noisy shared runner.

feature_generation.note: Runs once per bar per timeframe. The p99 is what matters: a slow tail here delays every decision behind it.

signal_generation.note: Model inference plus the meta-label pass.

risk_check.note: Sits between a signal and an order. Anything slow here is latency paid on every trade, and it must never be the reason somebody is tempted to bypass it.

order_placement.note: Dominated by the venue round trip, so the budget is generous and the error rate is the informative number. 1% covers ordinary venue flakiness; more than that is a venue problem worth halting for.

reconciliation.note: Runs at startup and on a schedule, not in the trading path.

api_status_endpoint.note: An operator refreshing a dashboard during an incident is the worst time for this to be slow.
